name: AI writing assistants
intro: Where AI actually helps you write, and where it is a thin ChatGPT wrapper.

apps.title: ChatGPT
apps.verdict: OpenAI's flagship AI assistant with broad capabilities for editing, rewriting, and structuring text. The main weakness: the model hallucinates on facts and loses context in long sessions.
apps.loved: Handles complex editing and style requests faster and more accurately than a search engine.
apps.weak: Memory between sessions is inconsistent and sometimes mixes another conversation's context into the current one.
apps.whoFor: Anyone who writes regularly and wants a general-purpose AI assistant

apps.title: iA Writer
apps.verdict: The best minimalist editor for serious writing on iOS: polished down to the details, supports Markdown, syncs with iCloud, and has been beloved by writers for over a decade. Downsides include occasional bugs with cloud folders and weak Arabic support.
apps.loved: Focus mode and typography create a working atmosphere that is hard to replicate in other apps.
apps.weak: Folders in Dropbox and third-party clouds occasionally disappear after updates.
apps.whoFor: Writers and journalists who need a distraction-free environment and Markdown

apps.title: Shortwave - AI Email
apps.verdict: Shortwave offers genuinely smart inbox organization with AI search and split folders, which sets it apart from ordinary email clients. Gmail-only support, no unified inbox, and limited compose formatting hold back a higher score.
apps.loved: AI search across your entire email history and automatic message grouping clear out inbox chaos.
apps.weak: No Outlook or other provider support, and you cannot bold text in a composed message.
apps.whoFor: Entrepreneurs and managers who live in Gmail and are overwhelmed by their inbox

apps.title: Paraphrase: Rewording Tool
apps.verdict: Does one thing — paraphrasing — and does it well enough: preserves meaning, changes phrasing, and works in Spanish. Limited on input length and sometimes sounds too textbook-like.
apps.loved: Simplicity: paste text, get a different version with no extra setup.
apps.weak: No choice of rephrasing style and a character limit on input length.
apps.whoFor: Students and office workers who need to quickly rewrite a paragraph

quotes.text: Love ! You say exactly what I want myself to sound like when I am in a ADHD rush!! I already rated this app, but I think you guys just want feedback and honestly for people with ADHD like honestly diagnosed ADHD you know nowadays everybody has ADHD that genuinely as a person with ADHD. This helps.

This app is very useful in so many different ways. The only thing that's holding back the 5th star is sometimes it sounds to textbook, however is that's something your aiming for that's right up your alley.

apps.title: Grammarly: AI Keyboard & Notes
apps.verdict: Grammarly remains a strong tool for real-time grammar and style checking, especially in keyboard mode. However, AI rephrasing often distorts meaning, and the aggressive paywall is frustrating.
apps.loved: Keyboard mode works directly in any app and highlights errors immediately.
apps.weak: AI tone-reframing changes the meaning of what you wrote instead of improving the form.
apps.whoFor: Native speakers who need a quick grammar checker

quotes.text: I do not wish for Grammarly AI to assist with my writing because of the many errors it makes by adding a word twice, changing the spelling of a word, and altering the intended meaning of the message. If AI is forced on me to use, I will close my account.

I love the Grammarly app, but there are a few things that drive me crazy. 1. It makes corrections where corrections aren't needed. Perfect example: In the first sentence of this review, I typed, "I love the Grammarly app." The app will tell me to remove the "the" before Grammarly.
Since I had my aneurysm and two strokes my communication has been texting and I lost my ability to write and put sentences together so yes this app is very important to me
A helpful app for a foreign speaker!!!

apps.title: Werdsmith: Writing App
apps.verdict: Werdsmith is a genuine writers' app with novel, screenplay, and poetry modes, a ghost-author feature for breaking creative blocks, and multi-device sync. For mobile fiction writing it is one of the better tools, though the paywall limits free use.
apps.loved: The next-sentence autocomplete genuinely helps break through a creative block without disrupting your style.
apps.weak: No way to split a novel into parts or manually control chapter numbers when inserting content.
apps.whoFor: Fiction writers who write regularly and on mobile

apps.title: Fortelling - Story Writing App
apps.verdict: Fortelling solves a real problem for writers: keeping characters, timelines, and world-building in one place. Crashes during account creation and an aggressive paywall undermine an otherwise solid experience.
apps.loved: Depth of world-building tools and the ability to get feedback from other writers.
apps.weak: Many essential organization features are locked behind a subscription.
apps.whoFor: Aspiring sci-fi and fantasy writers who need a mobile story organizer

apps.title: Google Gemini
apps.verdict: Google's AI assistant with a strong context window and deep integration with Google services, but it over-filters safety on neutral requests and hallucinates on facts.
apps.loved: Processes long documents quickly and summarizes large texts accurately.
apps.weak: Safety filters block legitimate requests involving scenes with conflict or violence.
apps.whoFor: Writers already in Google Workspace who want AI right there

apps.title: Pages: Create Documents
apps.verdict: Apple's word processor with good typography and smooth text input, but no serious AI editing tools. It does not compete with ChatGPT on writing assistance, though it beats any cloud editor on formatting.
apps.loved: Intuitive templates and multilingual support without extra setup.
apps.weak: Advanced formatting features are buried so deep that even experienced users cannot find them without outside help.
apps.whoFor: Apple users writing personal documents who do not want Microsoft Word

apps.title: Grok - AI Chat & Video
apps.verdict: XAI's assistant focused on free expression and real-time data from X. It handles grammar and text structure well, but value drops sharply once the free-plan limits run out.
apps.loved: Gives thorough answers on grammar and sentence structure without hedging.
apps.weak: Prompt limits on the paid plan run out very quickly when doing editing work.
apps.whoFor: Writers who value freedom of topic and fresh data from social media

apps.title: Claude by Anthropic
apps.verdict: Claude as a model is highly regarded for reasoning quality and writing assistance, but the mobile app is regularly criticized for instability, crashes, and poor support. The product is stronger on the web.
apps.loved: The quality of responses on text and nuance of phrasing is above most competitors.
apps.weak: The mobile app frequently freezes, loses chats, and is not adapted for assistive technologies.
apps.whoFor: Writers and developers who work through a browser

quotes.text: Claude is a genuinely cool AI, and the app allows for a lot. However, as a blind person using Voiceover, it takes a lot of effort to navigate. The Voiceover focus when reading back the chats is atrociouss. I have to swipe back and fourth just to read a response.

apps.title: DeepSeek - AI Assistant
apps.verdict: DeepSeek is a genuinely powerful reasoning model let down by an unstable mobile app: constant switches to Chinese and a regeneration limit frustrate even loyal users. The model is smarter than its wrapper.
apps.loved: The transparent chain of thought before each answer helps you understand how the AI reached its conclusion.
apps.weak: The app responds in Chinese even when the interface language is explicitly set, and this cannot be fixed in settings.
apps.whoFor: Researchers and students who care about the logic of reasoning

quotes.text: For context before I write this review, I've never wrote one of these. I use this app to make in depth stories for myself for whenever I'm bored. I write all the characters, their features, personalities and what they look like. For the first few months it was great.

apps.title: Ginger Writer
apps.verdict: Ginger Writer works as a grammar checker and rephraser, catches errors that Grammarly misses, and offers several rephrasing options. The interface feels dated, and there is no custom dictionary or keyboard extension for iOS.
apps.loved: Multiple rephrasing options make it quick to pick the best version.
apps.weak: Misses articles in simple sentences and does not support custom writing styles.
apps.whoFor: Non-native English speakers who need to check their English text

quotes.text: The app can not handle simple sentences such as: "I go to store." It can not notice the missing "the" required in English. So the app seems incapable of finding articles.
I have found this app to be very useful. In case I'm too lazy to write something elegant, I can simply type in the sentences and Ginger will give me multiple options to choose from.

apps.title: Daily Prompt: Writing Prompts
apps.verdict: Daily Prompt genuinely breaks creative blocks: users write things they would never have reached without a prompt. The publishing platform and comments bring a live audience, though adding AI-generated images angered part of the creative community.
apps.loved: Daily prompts and the ability to anonymously publish text and receive reader feedback.
apps.weak: Without a subscription you can barely save or continue anything, and AI art in prompts annoys writers.
apps.whoFor: Beginning writers and poets who need a nudge and a live community

apps.title: LearnEnglish Grammar (UK ed.)
apps.verdict: A solid grammar trainer from the British Council with a good exercise library, but with noticeable bugs in answer checking. It works as a passive practice tool, not as a writing assistant.
apps.loved: Structured rule-based exercises with clear level-by-level progress.
apps.weak: Does not explain why an answer is wrong and does not teach you to write natural prose.
apps.whoFor: People learning British English grammar as a second language

apps.title: Spike: AI Email & Team Chat
apps.verdict: Spike is an email client with a messenger-style interface and AI writing assistance, not a pure writing tool. AI-composed emails work, but the main value is read receipts and a chat wrapper over email.
apps.loved: The chat interface on top of email removes the feeling of dealing with a mailbox.
apps.weak: Search is limited to 60 days on the free plan, and there is no unified inbox without a subscription.
apps.whoFor: Freelancers and small teams handling business correspondence

apps.title: Quillbot-AI Writing & Keyboard
apps.verdict: QuillBot genuinely helps with paraphrasing and improving text, especially for non-native speakers. After recent updates, the quality of a second round of editing has degraded, and the free mode has become nearly worthless.
apps.loved: Natively paraphrases and finds better word choices so that text sounds more polished and precise.
apps.weak: A second round of editing often merges words and breaks sentences that were already correct.
apps.whoFor: Non-native speakers writing in English

quotes.text: Your app is great when it works on my phone - however, I am not sure if its a bug or do I have to give up my privacy and grant you a full access to my keyboard History and full access to my passwords and every single word ever written!!!! This is an invasion of privacy.
Not being a native speaker, and consequently, English is not my first spoken language, I have learned so much with QuillBot and the ways I could express myself.

I spent an hour writing something only for this app to glitch when correcting an error and delete half of what I wrote, it doesn't save drafts and there isn't an undo button. I'm very frustrated and will not be changing my review until an undo button is added.

apps.title: Spark Mail: AI Email Assistant
apps.verdict: Spark Mail used to be a strong email client with smart sorting, but after adding AI features it became unstable: emails fail to load and accounts get logged out. The AI writing assistant is secondary.
apps.loved: Smart inbox categorization and the snooze feature genuinely save time.
apps.weak: Adding an AI layer broke the basic reliability of email delivery and sync.
apps.whoFor: Users with multiple email accounts who need smart sorting

apps.title: Johnny Grammar Word Challenge
apps.verdict: British Council's Word Challenge game format is good for drilling grammar and spelling under a timer, but without error explanations it turns into pointless guessing.
apps.loved: The fast game format is engaging, especially for people who already know the basics.
apps.weak: Does not explain why an answer is wrong; learning without feedback is ineffective.
apps.whoFor: People who already know grammar and want to sharpen reaction speed

apps.title: Monica AI: Ultimate AI Assist
apps.verdict: Monica offers access to multiple language models in one place with a browser extension and cross-device sync, which is genuinely useful. The downside: models update slowly, support is silent, and the podcast TTS reads markup aloud.
apps.loved: A single interface for multiple models with chat history synced between iPhone and Mac saves time switching tools.
apps.weak: The app has not been updated for six months and is gradually losing its roster of current models.
apps.whoFor: Professionals who use several AI models every day

apps.title: Scrivener
apps.verdict: Scrivener on iOS was once a full-featured writing tool, but the mobile version has not been updated in a long time, key formatting features are broken, and Dropbox sync is unreliable. The desktop version remains strong.
apps.loved: Nested folders and binders let you organize even a complex multi-level project with hundreds of notes.
apps.weak: Font and style formatting crashes on every attempt, and the mobile app has gone years without critical fixes.
apps.whoFor: Novel writers who primarily work on Mac

apps.title: AI Writer - Writing Assistant
apps.verdict: The most capable tool in this group for genuine creative writing: helps with poetry, essays, and stories, and several users describe specific quality results. Proofreading of existing text is a weak spot.
apps.loved: Generates poetry and story openings with vivid imagery that users find unexpectedly good.
apps.weak: Proofreading and editing someone else's text is poorly implemented or does not work at all.
apps.whoFor: Aspiring writers and students who need help generating text from scratch

quotes.text: This program was a lifesaver for helping my 12 year old daughter with her essay for school. She has a learning disability and this program helped her put her words into a paper she was proud to turn in to her teacher.

apps.title: Notability: AI Notes & PDF app
apps.verdict: A handwritten notes app for Apple Pencil with an AI quiz-generation feature. A recent update changed how the Pencil works with no way to revert it and triggered a wave of users abandoning the app.
apps.loved: The AI quiz generator from notes genuinely helps students prepare for exams.
apps.weak: A critical update changed Apple Pencil behavior and removed the quick eraser switch with no alternative way to restore the old behavior.
apps.whoFor: Students with an iPad and Apple Pencil who need handwritten notes and AI review

apps.title: TypeAI: AI Keyboard & Writer
apps.verdict: A keyboard with AI correction and translation built directly into any app — a solid idea, but the execution has degraded: language conflicts, random resets, and an outdated knowledge base from October 2023. Value has dropped over two years.
apps.loved: Built-in translation right in the keyboard without switching apps.
apps.weak: When using two languages at once the app fights itself and constantly switches the language without being asked.
apps.whoFor: Bilingual users messaging in both languages

quotes.text: I bought the lifetime package and just found out today that the ai knowledge/ training stopped in October 2023… not good for a lifetime purchase!

I got this mainly for the auto reply feature. You need to copy the incoming message to your clipboard, which is ok but annoying. My main complaint is that there is a refresh button to regenerate the reply, but it isn't creative enough with the replies.

apps.title: Superhuman Mail
apps.verdict: Superhuman noticeably speeds up email work through keyboard shortcuts and AI email drafts, but the AI side is weak: meeting scheduler bugs and unstable MCP integration. The main value is UX speed, not generation quality.
apps.loved: Keyboard shortcuts genuinely cut down email processing time.
apps.weak: The AI meeting scheduler produces errors, and there is no unified inbox for multiple accounts.
apps.whoFor: Managers and founders with a high volume of business email

apps.title: Auri AI Keyboard & Assistant
apps.verdict: An AI keyboard assistant with a genuinely useful voice-note transcription and editing feature, but the predictive keyboard is slow and the daily limit runs out after two or three actions. A product with a seed of an idea in rough execution.
apps.loved: Transcribing and AI-polishing voice recordings produces cleaner output than Otter.
apps.weak: Predictive input is slow and the daily limit is too small for real work.
apps.whoFor: People who dictate notes and want clean text output

apps.title: AI Essay Writer - PaperMate
apps.verdict: The app delivers real value for essays and legal documents, but trial period behavior raises questions and the editor has no version history. The product works, but clearly falls short of web-based ChatGPT.
apps.loved: Helps structure and rephrase drafts, especially for academic texts.
apps.weak: No version history: one undo button rolls back all edits at once.
apps.whoFor: Students who need to quickly improve an essay draft

quotes.text: Amazing App helps me rewrite my ideas better and helps with citations correctly. Even helps with my dyslexia on my easy

apps.title: Answer.AI - Your AI tutor
apps.verdict: Answer.AI helps students solve standard math problems and read texts via the camera, but accuracy is inconsistent and the app often gives wrong answers. A learning tool, not a writing tool.
apps.loved: Camera scanning of problems and instant step-by-step solution breakdowns.
apps.weak: Writing and humanities answers are weak and frequently incorrect.
apps.whoFor: Students with math and science assignments

quotes.text: This app is so good I honestly am horrible in math and this has helped me do much, I used to get c and d but now I get a and b!

apps.title: Proofreader AI Grammar Checker
apps.verdict: Proofreader AI catches stylistic and grammatical errors and offers AI rewrites, but it imposes its own rules — removing adverbs with no alternatives — and does not support custom styles. Better than built-in Word, weaker than Grammarly.
apps.loved: AI rewriting raises the formal tone of business text.
apps.weak: No style settings; imposes a single template regardless of genre.
apps.whoFor: Authors of business letters and reports with no editing experience

quotes.text: During my trial of the Pro version, I tried it on some creative writing I've been working on. Wow! To be sure, it found some useful things and I appreciate that. The problem is that there are no settings to tell it what style you're trying to adhere to. You don't use the serial comma? Too bad!
Truth be told I don't see the difference between Proofreader and Microsoft Word spellchecker.

apps.title: Just Write - App For Writer
apps.verdict: A minimalist editor for storing drafts and chapters without distractions, but iCloud sync is unreliable and several users lost weeks of work. There is no AI component whatsoever.
apps.loved: Book and chapter folders, offline mode, and no ads in the basic version.
apps.weak: Cross-device sync breaks and destroys text with no way to recover it.
apps.whoFor: Beginning writers who need a simple offline journal

quotes.text: This app so desperately needs a sign in option besides the iCloud because I had to get a new iCloud and I lost all of my writing, I am so devastated.

apps.title: Microsoft Outlook
apps.verdict: Microsoft's email client, not an AI writing tool. Main complaints: email delivery delays measured in days, thread disorder, and accidental draft deletion.
apps.loved: On iPhone it runs smoothly and syncs the calendar with email in one interface.
apps.weak: Thread order cannot be adjusted and regularly confuses users when replying.
apps.whoFor: Corporate Microsoft 365 users on iPhone

apps.title: AI Writer: Email Letter Essay
apps.verdict: The app genuinely helps with essays and business letters at a basic level, but a request limit under an unlimited subscription and a clunky onboarding undermine trust. Real value is there but buried under opaque terms.
apps.loved: Helps put thoughts into words when nothing comes, especially for formal and business texts.
apps.weak: The unlimited subscription actually has a hidden rate limit with forced pauses between requests.
apps.whoFor: Students and professionals who occasionally need a letter or essay draft

quotes.text: This is an amazing app, especially when articulating is crucial and finding the right words to properly express yourself is just out of reach on that particular day :)
it really helps with essay and fanfics i write!

apps.title: MyStory.today
apps.verdict: MyStory offers a convenient structure for storing chapters, characters, and locations in one place. The main problem is not the AI features but data loss from missing auto-save and unreliable sync — critical for writers.
apps.loved: Book organization with nested scenes, character cards, and a cork board all in one project.
apps.weak: No reliable auto-save; users lose hours of work from an accidental screen tap.
apps.whoFor: Authors of fan fiction and amateur novels on their phone

quotes.text: I am paying for the premium version. The whole point of the app is to save your writing. It doesn't save every time. What on earth is going on. I've lost so much.
I've had books in here that I've kept over the span of 7 years, all for them to get completed deleted. Who do you think you are? Deleting my memories and childhood memories, I will never forget this.

apps.title: Grammar Fix
apps.verdict: A small ten-question multiple-choice trainer on basic grammar: useful for students and English learners, but not needed by professional writers. There is no text generation or real-time checking — not an AI Writing Assistant in any meaningful sense.
apps.loved: Quickly explains commonly confused rules like who/whom and there/their in a clear format.
apps.weak: Only 10 exercises; no additional content and no real writing tools.
apps.whoFor: Beginners in English who need basic rule practice

apps.title: AI Chat - Chatty.ai Chatbot
apps.verdict: Helps with resumes, study materials, and short text writing, but does not retain context between sessions — critical for long projects like a book. Works as a thin GPT bridge with no independent value.
apps.loved: Genuinely helps beginners write resumes and short structured texts.
apps.weak: Does not save conversation history, making work on longer texts impossible.
apps.whoFor: One-off tasks: resumes, letters, homework

apps.title: Wordtune: AI Writing Keyboard
apps.verdict: Wordtune was a useful keyboard paraphrasing tool, but after the 2024 redesign the core feature became unstable or disappeared entirely. Paying users are complaining broadly about a regression in suggestion quality.
apps.loved: Rephrasing variations directly in the keyboard without switching apps.
apps.weak: After the update the model picks worse suggestions than it did a year ago.
apps.whoFor: People who write a lot in messaging apps and want to quickly improve their tone

quotes.text: Takes over your keypad and causes auto correct to not work. It's a mess and a total waste of money. Also they will charge you $119 per year with this trash.
Wordtune has helped me write messages especially when I'm in a hurry. It has also helped rewrite some sentences to make it sound cleaner. Thanks Wordtune!

apps.title: ParagraphAI: Writer & Keyboard
apps.verdict: ParagraphAI works as a keyboard and template generator for letters and paragraphs, and at its best it genuinely sped up business correspondence. Keyboard shaking, post-iOS-update breakage, and no prompt history make daily use unreliable.
apps.loved: Reworks the tone of a message and fixes grammar right in the keyboard without switching apps.
apps.weak: The keyboard trembles and glitches on recent iOS versions, and prompt history is not saved.
apps.whoFor: People who write a lot of business email from their phone

quotes.text: First f all i am loving the app but i am blind and unable to adjust the sliders to affect the output. The rest of the app works great with voiceover except for the sliders I am unable to change the values at all.
I must say, this app is truly remarkable! It offers fantastic communication tools, particularly when it comes to sending messages and emails with impeccable grammar. It's truly a remarkable tool.

apps.title: AI Chatbot & Writer: KnowIt
apps.verdict: A thin GPT wrapper with category templates: works well when it works, but servers go down regularly and responses are outdated (it calls the M1 the "latest chip"). Real added value over direct ChatGPT is minimal.
apps.loved: Categorized templates help you frame a request quickly without writing long prompts.
apps.weak: Servers go down too often for a paid tool, sometimes for days.
apps.whoFor: Users who want structured access to GPT without configuring prompts

quotes.text: I've been using this application for 2 years now, and greatly appreciate the assistance I get. For only $40 annually, I revert to this app often when needing assistance with tough professional communications.

apps.title: Chat AI: Chatbot, Writing Bot
apps.verdict: A basic chat wrapper with no original product layer: helps with emails and brainstorming, but regularly loses context and applies heavy censorship to legitimate tasks. Nobody specifically praises the text quality apart from the mere existence of AI.
apps.loved: You can just talk and get things off your chest without judgment.
apps.weak: Censors legitimate work tasks like writing code, is unstable, and degrades with updates.
apps.whoFor: People who need a conversational companion, not a writing tool

apps.title: Author AI: Book Creator
apps.verdict: Author AI generates a book structure and chapters from given parameters, but the text is mechanical: genre tags end up in the prose, chapters are short at around five paragraphs, and context is lost after chapter ten. Not suitable for serious authoring.
apps.loved: Helps overcome the fear of a blank page and get a story started.
apps.weak: The model loses the plot thread by chapter ten and repeats the same phrases.
apps.whoFor: Beginning writers who need a starter scaffold for a story

quotes.text: The app tries to change you story or add extra stuff that isn't wanted. If you make a book more than ten chapters it will forget events that have already happened
It repeats the same wording in several chapters. Doesn't appear to be able to export the book for publication.

apps.title: Grammar Check Corrector by AI
apps.verdict: A Grammarly clone with aggressive monetization: the free check is effectively inaccessible without watching an ad or buying a subscription, and some users could not use a paid subscription they had already bought. Almost no independent value.
apps.loved: The interface is clear enough for students who want to check homework.
apps.weak: After paying for access the app continues to show ads or throws errors.
apps.whoFor: Nobody — better to download the original Grammarly

apps.title: Chat AI: Ask Chatbot Answers
apps.verdict: Another generic chatbot wrapper that has degraded with updates: the core function of answering questions stopped working for paying users. Helps with social media and emails when it works.
apps.loved: Quickly generates posts and letters for small businesses using ready-made templates.
apps.weak: After an update it stops understanding basic commands even for paying users.
apps.whoFor: Small business owners who need templated copy

apps.title: Gmail - Email by Google
apps.verdict: Google's email client with no AI writing features. Reviews describe freezing, update loops, and an inability to sort mail properly.
apps.loved: Cross-platform sync and a reliable spam filter work consistently.
apps.weak: The app freezes after opening several emails in a row and needs a restart.
apps.whoFor: Users in the Google ecosystem who need integration with Drive and Meet

apps.title: AI Song Music Generator: Muzio
apps.verdict: A text-to-music generator with a claimed voice-cloning feature that in practice does not work or behaves erratically. Style input is ignored, lyrics repeat, and the output is predictably uniform.
apps.loved: The first couple of experimental tracks generate excitement in people with no music production experience.
apps.weak: The app ignores the selected genre and makes all tracks sound the same.
apps.whoFor: A casual user with no musical skills who needs one or two songs

apps.title: Grammar AI Checker & Corrector
apps.verdict: A basic grammar checker with a simple interface that works for simple punctuation fixes. Very few genuine reviews of grammar check quality; instead there are complaints about text loss and slowdowns after updates.
apps.loved: No email required at registration and works without unnecessary steps for a quick spelling check.
apps.weak: Cutting and pasting text can delete all your work with no undo option.
apps.whoFor: Users who need a quick check on a short piece of text

quotes.text: La aplicación ha sufrido un deterioro notable tras la actualización, ya que el corrector sistemáticamente cambia el tono de mis mensajes a melancólico cuando intento expresar algo positivo, lo que me hace considerar seriamente cancelar mi suscripción.

Just when I was about to feel satisfied with this app, I did a "cut" to rearrange my own words and when I did paste to where I wanted to insert text, the whole writing page disappeared! There is no undo to bring back the 1000+ words I have typed. SO FRUSTRATING!!!

apps.title: TextAI - AI Texting Assistant
apps.verdict: A niche tool for rephrasing messages and emails into a professional tone — a narrow but real job. The product is discredited by complaints about fraudulent charges via a third-party provider called Flirtonic.
apps.loved: Helps people who struggle to express themselves write confident messages and emails.
apps.weak: Does not honor key user instructions and removes desired content from the rewritten text.
apps.whoFor: People who find it hard to put thoughts into words in written communication

apps.title: CorrectMe Grammar AI Keyboard
apps.verdict: CorrectMe looks useful on paper as an AI editor built into the keyboard, but chronic instability after iOS updates makes it unreliable. A 500-word limit and frequent failures cancel out the claimed value.
apps.loved: When it works correctly it delivers corrections ranging from basic to professional style right in the input field.
apps.weak: Often stops working after an iOS update and has no proper support to restore access.
apps.whoFor: iPhone users writing short messages who need quick style fixes

apps.title: Writely - AI Keyboard & Writer
apps.verdict: An AI keyboard with rephrasing, but it lags while typing, does not support swipe input, duplicates text on paste, and requires full keyboard access. Rephrasing quality is mediocre according to real users.
apps.loved: Changing tone directly in the keyboard without switching apps is a convenient idea.
apps.weak: Lags during fast typing and autocorrect inserts capital letters in the middle of words.
apps.whoFor: People who need quick tone fixes in messaging apps

quotes.text: It doesn't have a lot of features of that you can make your paragraph short or you can make it intense or you can make it friendly it just don't give you those options know it's just it's just basic
If this keyboard had swiping functionality, it would be my favorite keyboard to use. I prefer to swipe on the keyboard instead of having to touch every key.

apps.title: Chatbot AI - Smart Search Bot
apps.verdict: Another GPT wrapper with a knowledge base outdated to October 2023 and image generation that cannot handle simple prompts. Nearly useless for writing tasks.
apps.loved: Initial responses to structured requests such as construction topics are sometimes detailed.
apps.weak: Image generation even with a clear prompt produces random irrelevant output.
apps.whoFor: A user who needs a simple text answer once a week

quotes.text: Definitely not ready for public release. This feels like a cheap beta. A cheap AI app that in 6 months will be inactive leaving the app abondoned and loosing your $60 bucks pay once options.
Great tool but the data is only current to October 2023 don't is often useless

apps.title: Writey Cursive Handwriting
apps.verdict: The app teaches cursive and calligraphic handwriting, but basic features require payment, pressure sensitivity is inconsistent, and left-hand support is absent despite being advertised. A useful exercise library is killed by a poor UX and aggressive paywall.
apps.loved: Visible letter samples with step-by-step tracing help children learn cursive from scratch.
apps.weak: Stroke recognition is poorly calibrated and does not account for different pen-holding techniques.
apps.whoFor: Parents teaching children handwriting, if they are willing to pay

apps.title: Humanize AI: Paraphrase Tools
apps.verdict: Humanize AI is supposed to rewrite AI-generated text into a human style, but real reviews document extra dashes being added, volume being padded, and meaningless substitutions. AI detectors continue to flag the output.
apps.loved: Makes minor surface-level changes to AI text phrasing.
apps.weak: Rephrasing adds unnecessary constructions and does not pass AI detectors.
apps.whoFor: Students looking for a quick AI-detector bypass, though it does not work

quotes.text: Please for the love of god stop using em dashes and making the paragraph unnecessarily longer making me regret paying money for this
My professors have never flagged me for AI thanks to this app

Ok so when I purchased this originally it was spot on. A few weeks later I don't know what's happening but if the humanized part is supposed to help reword why when I upload it to ai detector it's still 75 % can be seen?

apps.weak: Replies sound unnatural and need manual editing before sending.

apps.whoFor: Nobody: ChatGPT does the same thing for free without hidden charges

apps.weak: No writing specialization at all — just a chatbot with marketing positioning.

apps.weak: Weak and predictable model avoids uncomfortable questions and changes the subject instead of answering.
apps.whoFor: Users with basic needs for fixing short messages

apps.title: AI Chatbot with Сhat - Chatrun

apps.weak: Text rephrasing and writing assistance produce weak, inaccurate output even for paying users.

apps.title: Mail
apps.verdict: Apple's built-in email client, unrelated to AI writing. Written reviews document undelivered emails, broken search, and accidental deletion of conversations.

apps.title: Email - Edison Mail
apps.verdict: Edison Mail is an email client, not an AI writing assistant. Product quality has dropped: frequent logouts, broken search, and disappearing emails make it unreliable.

apps.weak: Emails disappear, search is broken, and accounts regularly get logged out for no apparent reason.
apps.whoFor: Users who want to combine multiple inboxes for free

apps.title: AI+ Chat & Al Video Generator

apps.weak: Image generation systematically ignores the prompt and produces irrelevant output.

apps.title: Write This - AI Text Generator
apps.verdict: A thin ChatGPT wrapper with no original writing or editing mechanics. Users complain about duplicate charges and a dated interface, and substantive reviews of generation quality are nearly absent.
